observations.text:
Edda unfolds the question you drafted but never submitted. There is no search result attached to it. She moves her cup to make a second place at the table.

"Stay a minute. You don't have to bring me an answer to sit here."

Her cup leaves a pale ring on the table. The rain goes on.

choices.text:
1
Stay for the minute she offered. Then go back.

observations.text:
You leave the wall to the weather. The leak you already made can live without your voice on this wall.

Sera does not chase you. Ward Nine has practice at people who get to the stair and then remember they have somewhere dry to be. The names stay. The rain stays. You stay a person who could have spoken and did not, which is its own title.

Halfway down the stair you hear Sera set the pencil against the next line. She does not ask you to turn around. Her voice reaches you through the rain.

You remember the minute you stayed with Edda. No one asked you for a sentence to put on a wall.

"Mind the broken step. It's the second one down."

observations.text:
The received case is closed beside Kerr. He folds the recipient docket once, carefully, and places it on top. He keeps his hand there after the paper stops moving.

"Leave the case there. I need a minute before we talk about anything else."

You let the minute pass.

choices.text:
1
Let the quiet stand. Return to the collection account.

observations.text:
You tell Sera the leak already started. A second copy is loose. The tower bought one fire and did not get to own the other. You confirmed the leak out loud. That sentence is now on the wall beside the names.

She writes Replay under the last name, small, like a footnote that refuses to be one. It is not absolution. It is a witness who arrived late and said so out loud.

Sera does not draw a line from your name to the names above it. She leaves the space between them. When she sees you looking, she waits.

You remember the space beside Kerr's table. What reached it, and what did not, stays with you here.

"Your name can stay. Leave theirs where they are."

The case you handed over is still closed. Kerr clears a space beside the table leg. He does not try the brace or tell you how a fitting will go. For once, he points somewhere that is not a door.

"Put it beside the table leg. I can reach it from here."

You let the minute pass.

observations.text:
Ives closes the memorial list into the folio like it was always a Helion document that had been stored in the rain by mistake. Sera keeps the pencil. She does not keep the page.

Her private witness ledger stays on the stair. The archive original stays with Sera under its recorded source terms. Taking the memorial page opens no separately held source to Ives.

Replay is still on file. Ward Nine is now a line item under resolved, which is the word the tower uses when it means owned.

Ives opens the clasp again to free a corner of the page. Behind his shoulder, Sera places a fresh blank sheet beneath her pencil. Neither of them writes on it.

You remember the space beside Kerr's table. What reached it, and what did not, stays with you here.

"Mind the edge. Keep that page in one piece."

observations.text:
Edda sets the question beside the issuing-key result you actually obtained. She touches the cancellation line, then takes her hand off the paper. Mara's separate approval remains where it was.

"Put the reader away. I want to hear the rain for a minute."

Her cup leaves a pale ring on the table. The rain goes on.

choices.text:
1
Stay for the minute she offered. Then go back.

observations.text:
You read what the chair tried to file away. Three hundred is a number. The wall wants them one at a time.

You said them. Sera's pencil does not ask whether you meant to.

Above this hour, the city already titled the job Two Fires. This one is smaller and harder: a pencil, a wall, and your mouth doing a thing the tower cannot edit after the fact.

Rain reaches the lower edge of the names. Sera moves her hand down and leaves her pencil still until you finish. Then she looks at the place where your voice stopped.

You remember the minute you stayed with Edda. No one asked you for a sentence to put on a wall.

"Wait. Let me hear that one again."
